dcd87a9a084f247f.title: Conbi 400 Tablet
dcd87a9a084f247f.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, and B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and lowered physical strength during or after illness; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.); and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
dcd87a9a084f247f.usage:
Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
dcd87a9a084f247f.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 3 months of age; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: children who get plenty of sunlight and eat normal meals; premature infants, infants; infants under 1 year of age.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values.

Do not take together with levodopa.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools, diarrhea, stomatitis, loss of appetite, or abdominal bloating occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins B1, B2, and B6 and relieves neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, beriberi, and eye fatigue
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, and recovery, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), beriberi, eye fatigue

e55029e58e935586.title: Ginocal Tablet
e55029e58e935586.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for calcium deficiency and general calcium supply; to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age; and to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets.
e55029e58e935586.usage:
Adults: take 2 tablets at bedtime; if more is needed, take 1 tablet in the morning and 1 in the afternoon, then 2 tablets at bedtime.
Do not exceed 4 tablets per day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
e55029e58e935586.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of unknown cause affecting the whole body); kidney disease; kidney stones; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: premature infants, infants; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; past kidney stones.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with cardiac glycosides, vitamin D, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies calcium and vitamin D and prevents poor development of bones and teeth and rickets
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Calcium deficiency and calcium supply, vitamin D supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, growth periods, and old age, poor development of bones and teeth, prevention of rickets

f6e8a80a6142d012.title: Magferol Soft Capsule
f6e8a80a6142d012.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin E in old age; to relieve peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet; and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
f6e8a80a6142d012.usage:
Adolescents aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
f6e8a80a6142d012.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 12 months of age; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: premature infants, infants; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or conditions requiring careful use of lipid emulsions; conditions at particular risk from fat overload; a predisposition to thrombosis (blocked blood vessels).

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash (flushing), red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), reduced central nervous system function, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamin E and relieves peripheral circulatory disturbance, menopausal symptoms, and muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Vitamin E supply in old age, peripheral circulatory disturbance, menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of hands and feet, cold hands and feet, muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency

fd5f1cd5a031ef34.title: Anemo Tablet
fd5f1cd5a031ef34.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and sour belching.
fd5f1cd5a031ef34.usage:
Adults: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times daily between meals and at bedtime.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
fd5f1cd5a031ef34.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients on dialysis; breastfeeding women; children aged 7 years or younger; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; allergic constitution; past allergic symptoms (rash, flushing, itching, etc.); kidney disorder; pregnant or possibly pregnant women; people on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with gastrointestinal analgesic-antispasmodic agents or tetracycline antibiotics.

If rash, flushing, itching, or, rarely, dry mouth, constipation, or diarrhea occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Neutralizes stomach acid and relieves excess acid, heartburn, and related stomach symptoms
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching

01108ff74e6e7b6b.title: Hemo-Q Plus Capsule
01108ff74e6e7b6b.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia.
01108ff74e6e7b6b.usage:
Adults: take 1 capsule once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
01108ff74e6e7b6b.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism); hemosiderosis; non-iron-deficiency anemia; folic acid deficiency; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have any of the following: gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Overdose in children aged 6 years or younger may cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If allergic symptoms such as erythema (red spots), skin disorders, itching, general malaise, or bronchial breathing difficulty, or hives, photosensitivity reactions, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, coma, nausea, loss of appetite, weight loss, swelling, constipation, black stools, or stomach discomfort occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies iron to prevent and treat iron-deficiency anemia
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia

04a7b05964026d3c.title: Shinil Thiamine HCl Tablet 10 mg
04a7b05964026d3c.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of vitamin B1 deficiency; to supply vitamin B1 when dietary intake is insufficient due to increased demand, such as in wasting diseases, hyperthyroidism, pregnancy and breastfeeding, or heavy physical labor; and for Wernicke encephalopathy, beriberi, and muscle pain, joint pain, neuralgia, peripheral neuritis, and peripheral nerve palsy presumed to involve vitamin B1 deficiency or metabolic disorder.
04a7b05964026d3c.usage:
Adults: take 1 to 10 mg at a time, 1 to 3 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
04a7b05964026d3c.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If symptoms do not improve or worsen after about 1 month of use, consult a pharmacist.

If fever, itching, hives, lethargy, sweating, nausea, cyanosis, respiratory edema, or gastrointestinal bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamin B1 to prevent and treat deficiency and related nerve and muscle symptoms
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Prevention and treatment of vitamin B1 deficiency, supply during increased demand, Wernicke encephalopathy, beriberi, muscle pain, joint pain, neuralgia, peripheral neuritis, peripheral nerve palsy related to vitamin B1 deficiency

04e3106abeda9529.title: B-Max Active Tablet
04e3106abeda9529.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; for beriberi and eye fatigue; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; and to supply zinc.
04e3106abeda9529.usage:
Adolescents aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
04e3106abeda9529.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypercalcemia; sarcoidosis; kidney disease; hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or if any of the following applies: children who get plenty of sunlight and eat normal meals; hyperoxaluria; premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; gout; kidney stones or past kidney stones; folic acid deficiency; a predisposition to thrombosis.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values, or interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests.

While taking this medicine, do not take phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (flushing), loose stools, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, E and zinc, relieves neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, and oral and skin inflammation, and prevents poor development of bones and teeth and rickets
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, recovery, growth periods, and old age, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, beriberi, eye fatigue, poor development of bones and teeth, prevention of rickets, zinc supply

07dbd97e86802a37.title: Artize Tablet
07dbd97e86802a37.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, food stagnation, promotion of digestion, and upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion.
07dbd97e86802a37.usage:
Adults aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
07dbd97e86802a37.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: children aged 7 years or younger; hypersensitivity or past allergic reaction to soybean oil; hypersensitivity to soybeans or peanuts.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or conditions requiring careful use of lipid emulsions; allergic constitution; conditions at particular risk from fat overload.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Promotes digestion and relieves indigestion and related stomach symptoms
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, food stagnation, promotion of digestion, upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion

2342fd0e35e3234c.title: Ucobig Forte Tablet
2342fd0e35e3234c.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age; to relieve dry eyes and night blindness; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; to relieve pigmentation (freckles, dark spots) caused by sunlight or skin disease; to prevent gum bleeding and nosebleeds; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (lower back, shoulder stiffness, etc.); for beriberi and eye fatigue; for the prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia; and to supply zinc.
2342fd0e35e3234c.usage:
Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
2342fd0e35e3234c.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: women within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant (taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations); hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of unknown cause affecting the whole body); kidney disease; hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism); hemosiderosis; non-iron-deficiency anemia; kidney stones; severe renal failure; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Overdose in children aged 6 years or younger may cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values.

Consult a pharmacist before taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (flushing), loose stools, stomatitis, hives, photosensitivity reactions, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6, C, zinc, and iron, and is used for eye, bone, and skin symptoms and iron-deficiency anemia
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, recovery, growth periods, and old age, dry eyes, night blindness, poor development of bones and teeth, prevention of rickets, pigmentation (freckles, dark spots), prevention of gum bleeding and nosebleeds, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, beriberi, eye fatigue, prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia, zinc supply
